text:
Ashley L: thinking aloud — for A/B canaries do we want a lightweight sidecar (judger) next to the router that can fast-fail on latency/quality, or keep fallback decisions in the central control plane?
Zane P: +1 to exploring sidecar. main benefit i see is <100ms local decisions during network partition.
Taylor M: sidecar is tempting but state-sync surfaces are hairy. how do we keep the judger's decision deterministic across restarts?
Samira R: what signal set are we using? latency p95, token-timeouts, inference error rate? we need to be careful mixing quality signals with infra signals.
Ashley L: agreed. initial MVP signals: p95 latency, 500/5xx ratio, and a simple semantic-quality regression flag (from async evals).
Zane P: sketch of sidecar config:
```
# sidecar config (proposal)
judger:
  lookback: 30s
  signals: [latency_p95, http_5xx_rate, async_eval_regression]
  threshold:
    latency_p95_ms: 300
    http_5xx_rate: 0.01
  action: fallback_to:alternate_model
```
Taylor M: who owns the model variant routing list? if sidecar decides to fallout, it needs a compatible fallback target list from control plane. otherwise it may pick a bad variant.
Samira R: we could bundle a compact routing policy blob (signed) with each judger deployment. control plane rotates it on rollout. sidecar verifies signature before applying.
Ashley L: nice — that keeps control plane authoritative while enabling local decisions. also avoids chatty RPCs.
Infra Bot: note: adding local fallbacks increases complexity for canary observability — ensure traces include "judger.decision" spans.
Zane P: rollout idea: start with passive-only sidecar (decides and logs but doesn't route), then opt-in for emergency-only, then full auto.
Taylor M: what about multi-tenant routers? can a sidecar safely decide per-tenant? might need tenant-scoped thresholds.
Samira R: yes, thresholds should be per-tenant or per-cohort. cheap heuristic: default global thresholds + per-tenant overrides for high-SLA customers.
Ashley L: ops/incident playbook snippet:
- passive mode: sidecar logs decisions to /canary/judger/passive
- emergency mode: sidecar flips traffic to fallback but notifies control plane
- auto mode: sidecar flips and updates control plane with a compact event
DeployBot: deploy event: canary-sidecar v0.1 deployed to router-prod-3 in us-west-2 by taylor (1754209925) :rocket:
Zane P: one more thought — KV-cache warmup mismatch. when sidecar switches to fallback model, we might get a cold-kv penalty. lazy-copying KV is possible but messy. need to annotate expectations.
Taylor M: we should add a decay window: if sidecar flips more than N times in M minutes, escalate to control-plane rollback. avoids flip-flop.
Samira R: set N=3, M=10min as starting point. also emit metric judger.flip_count.
Ashley L: next steps: Taylor to prototype sidecar passive mode + signed policy blob. Zane to draft security review for signed blobs. Samira to map tenant threshold table. I'll collate into a short RFC follow-up.
Taylor M: ack, will have prototype by EOD Friday for a limited subset of routes.
Zane P: will start security writeup tomorrow.
Samira R: i'll prepare metric/dashboard template for the judger.
Ashley L: thanks team :thumbsup: this keeps control-plane intent but buys us faster SLO-friendly fallback.
Infra Bot: reminder: add trace annotations "judger.policy_id" and "judger.mode" before prod flip.
DeployBot: canary-sidecar v0.1 passive traffic started on router-prod-3 at 1754209940
Ashley L: filing RFC follow-up with notes and links to the prototype thread.
